sourcing_note: Follow-up to newly-sourced-batch-10.json: after sourcing 3 candidates for the REGULATORY/2018, REGULATORY/2019 and REGULATORY/2024 slots identified by the original greedy simulation, re-running the exact same dry-run against the updated real pool showed the selected-cohort negative count reached 39, not the predicted 40 - the non-linear RNG-cascading effect documented in the same simulation (adding real candidates with different candidate_id/issuer_id values than the simulation's placeholder IDs perturbs the shuffle differently) meant one of the three additions landed one negative short of the target. Re-ran the greedy search against the actual post-batch-10 pool and it identified several equally-good alternative single-slot fixes, including REGULATORY/2022 (2 real candidates tried and rejected on floor failures: AKBA on price, CRMD on liquidity) before REGULATORY/2021 (Ardelyx) confirmed as a clean pass. CORRECTION (see newly-sourced-batch-13.json for the full account): the re-verification described above was an isolated single-candidate-addition dry-run, not a full end-to-end selected-set diff against the real pool. When actually committed, ARDX landed in the same (stratum, year) bucket - REGULATORY/2021 - as an already-selected negative candidate (REG-2021-OMER-NARSOPLIMAB-CRL); the RNG cascade this addition triggered displaced OMER from the selected set, a like-for-like negative-for-negative swap with zero net gain (selected-cohort negative count stayed at 39, confirmed via a corrected full-selection-diff methodology). ARDX remains a genuine, floor-passing, well-documented negative candidate and is kept in the pool; the gap-closing work continued in batch-12 (LQDA) and batch-13 (KURA).

events.indication: control of serum phosphorus in chronic kidney disease patients on dialysis
events.notes: FDA CRL for tenapanor (CKD-on-dialysis phosphorus control) received 2021-07-28, publicly announced by the issuer 2021-07-29. The 8-K states the FDA agreed the data were 'effective' but characterized the treatment-effect magnitude as 'small and of unclear clinical significance,' requiring an additional trial - an efficacy-magnitude rejection with 'no safety, clinical pharmacology/biopharmaceutics, chemistry, manufacturing, and controls or non-clinical issues identified,' i.e. a genuine NDA rejection, not a CMC-only or mixed disclosure.
